data.content_ref: inline:The target's mechanism describes variance reduction via wisdom-of-the-crowd cancellation of random errors, but it never identifies the evidence within a single evaluation that would distinguish a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer — the second half of the problem. The counterconditions merely list when the mechanism fails (correlated bias, omitted variables) but do not specify the diagnostic evidence that separates true causal reliability (independent errors cancelling) from spurious agreement (shared heuristic shortcut that merely co-occurs with correct answers). A single evaluation showing high panel accuracy and checklist adherence is equally consistent with 'genuine variance reduction through independent judgments' and 'shared superficial compliance with a checklist that tracks surface features correlated with the right answer'; the target provides no discriminating evidence criterion, so it answers only the first half of the problem.
